headline: Microsoft disrupts EvilTokens account-theft platform
summary: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit disrupted the EvilTokens phishing platform, which had compromised more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts at over 10,000 organizations.

claims.statement: Microsoft disrupted the EvilTokens platform that compromised over 12,000 Microsoft accounts.

sources.quote: The EvilTokens platform that compromised more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts
Microsoft disrupts AI-assisted platform that compromised 12,000 accounts

claims.statement: The takedown was led by Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit and affected over 10,000 organizations.

sources.quote: at over 10,000 organizations has been disrupted in an effort led by Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit (DCU)

claims.statement: Ars Technica describes EvilTokens as an end-to-end, AI-assisted platform that made mass account compromises faster and easier.

sources.quote: EvilTokens provided an end-to-end platform that makes mass compromises faster and easier.
